# Format of `config/teams.yaml`

<!-- GENERATED by taxidermist from taxonomy/. Do not hand-edit: edit the schema and run `taxidermist docs`. -->

One entry per top-level key, each with the fields below. The key matches `^[a-z][a-z-]*$`. The team's short name, lowercase with dashes.

## Copy this

```yaml
<name>:
  purpose: <str>
  lead: <str>
  topics: [<garden | hiring | house | infra>]   # optional
```

## What to put in each field

**`purpose`** · required · `str`  
What the team is for, in one line.

**`lead`** · required · `str`  
The person page slug of whoever leads it.

Values: any page under [`people/`](../../people/), by its filename without `.md`. Checked, so a name that resolves to no page is a fault.

**`topics`** · optional · `list`  
The topics the team owns.

Values: `garden` · `hiring` · `house` · `infra`, defined below.

## What the values mean

### `topics`

Shared vocabulary from [../vocabularies/topic.yaml](../vocabularies/topic.yaml).

| value | group | means | not for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `garden` | home | Anything that grows. |  |
| `hiring` | work | Recruiting, interviews, onboarding. |  |
| `house` | home | Repairs and the things that break. |  |
| `infra` | work | Servers, deploys, the build. | Hiring for the infra team; that is `hiring`. |

## Adding a value

A field's `definitions` keys **are** its allowed values, so a value cannot exist until someone writes down what it means. Prefer an existing one, because a near-synonym fragments every filter. If nothing fits, add it to the right file under [taxonomy/](../README.md) with its one line, in the same change that uses it. `taxidermist check` fails otherwise.
